claim: KLIA Ekspres runs every 20 minutes between KL Sentral and KLIA T1 in 28 minutes (33 min to T2), with 10% off when bought via the app/website.
quote: The journey time between KL Sentral and KLIA T1 is 28 minutes, and 3 minutes between KLIA T1 and KLIA T2... KLIA Ekspres service currently runs every 20 minutes all day, every day

claim: The KL TravelPass bundles a one-way KLIA Ekspres ride with 2 days of unlimited rides on RapidKL LRT, MRT, Monorail and BRT.
quote: KL TravelPass | Unlimited Rides for 2 Days | KLIA Ekspres

claim: Rapid KL operates an integrated network covering MRT (Kajang and Putrajaya lines), LRT (Kelana Jaya, Ampang, Sri Petaling), KL Monorail and BRT Sunway under one fare table.
KL's rail and bus services run daily from roughly 6am to midnight, and Touch 'n Go cardholders get a cheaper cashless fare than cash buyers.
quote: rail and bus services operating 7 days a week from 6am to 12am... Touch 'n Go Card users enjoy lower 'Cashless Fare Rate' compared to 'Cash Fare Rate'

claim: Grab is the dominant ride-hail option from KLIA to the city, with in-app booking and cash or card payment.
quote: Grab has many services available for transport to KLIA or airport transfer in Kuala Lumpur

claim: Grab fares from KLIA to central KL typically run RM65 minimum and up to RM110+ during peak times, versus the 33-minute KLIA Ekspres.
quote: Grab prices from the airport to the city is minimum RM65 ($13.81 USD) going up to RM110 and possible more during peak times

claim: Bukit Bintang is KL's most popular tourist base for shopping, nightlife and Jalan Alor street food; KLCC is more upscale and walkable to the Petronas Towers.
quote: Bukit Bintang is the most popular and central area to stay in Kuala Lumpur with excellent hotels, restaurants, and world-class shopping malls

claim: KLCC, Bukit Bintang and the surrounding Golden Triangle concentrate most tourist activity, with Bangsar a quieter expat-leaning alternative.
quote: Much of tourist and commercial activity is centered around the 'Golden Triangle,' a core area consisting of KLCC, Bukit Bintang, and surrounding areas

claim: June in KL averages a high of around 32.3°C and a low of 23.2°C and is one of the drier months despite ~130mm of rain over ~12 days.
quote: an average high-temperature of a tropical 32.3°C (90.1°F), with a consistent average low-temperature of 23.2°C (73.8°F)

claim: Humidity in KL in June sits between 85% and 89%, making the heat feel oppressive even on dry days.
quote: Throughout June, humidity in Kuala Lumpur fluctuates between 85% and 89%

claim: Mosques and many temples require covered shoulders and knees; women need long sleeves, long bottoms and a headscarf, and robes are typically lent free on site.
quote: Women must wear long pants or skirts, long-sleeved tops, and a headscarf. Robes are available for loan if your attire is not suitable

claim: Upscale KL sky bars and restaurants typically enforce smart casual: collared shirts, dress pants and closed-toe shoes for men; no ripped jeans, athletic wear or flip-flops.
quote: The general dress code for sky bars in Kuala Lumpur tends to lean towards smart casual or business casual... ripped jeans, athletic wear, flip-flops, and overly casual attire are a no-go

claim: SkyBar at Traders Hotel explicitly bars shorts, sleeveless shirts, swimwear, gym-wear and slippers/flip-flops at the door.
quote: guests wearing shorts, sleeveless shirts, bathrobes, swimwear, gym-wear, pyjamas, and slippers (including bedroom slipper and flip-flops) will not be permitted entry

claim: KL is generally safe for tourists but motorbike-borne bag-snatching is the headline risk, concentrated around Bukit Bintang, Petaling Street and quieter LRT stations after dark.
quote: Motorcycle snatch thefts targeting handbags are more common than confrontational muggings... Hotspots for these types of thefts include Bukit Bintang, Petaling Street, and quieter stretches near some LRT stations after dark

claim: KL tap water is treated to national standards but most visitors stick to bottled or filtered water due to pipe-infrastructure contamination risk.
quote: tap water in Kuala Lumpur is treated and generally meets Malaysia's national drinking water quality standards... for safety it is advisable to consume boiled, filtered, or bottled water

claim: Touch 'n Go cards are the standard tap-to-pay product across LRT, MRT, Monorail and BRT and can be bought at the NU Sentral hub next to KL Sentral.
